2. Both the BMTC as well as the claimants are in appeal.
3. BMTC contends that the accident occurred solely due the negligence of the driver of the car and therefore, it ought not to be made liable for the compensation.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants contend that the charge sheet had been laid down against the driver of the BMTC bus and he has in fact admitted in the cross-examination that he had not lodged any counter complaint and this by itself prove the negligence of the driver of the BMTC bus.
It is also argued that the sums awarded by the Tribunal were inadequate.
5. The driver of the BMTC bus was examined as RW.1.
During the course of his examination-in-chief, he has contended that the accident occurred as the driver of the Maruti Zen Car drove the car in a negligent manner.
He has however, admitted that police have laid the charge sheet against him and more importantly he has admitted that he had not lodged any counter complaint against the driver of the car.
6. In my view, in the light of these facts, the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that the driver of the BMTC bus was responsible for the accident.
As a consequence, the appeals by BMTC challenging the negligence attributed to its driver are dismissed.
7. As far as the compensation is concerned, the claimant in MFA No.1785/2019 states that he is a practicing advocate and the Tribunal has erred in taking his income at Rs.6,000/-.

In my view,
